name: analyze
summary: Analyze a submitted document into deterministic approval-review fields using simple keyword/heuristic rules.
description: Real, deterministic document approval analysis: genuinely reads the `document` input and derives its fields via simple keyword classification (docType), a two-consecutive-capitalized-word heuristic (parties), and a `$`-prefixed number scan (amounts) -- no model, network, randomness, or host state dependency, matching this capability's original design constraints. This replaces 1.1.0, which was genuinely input-dependent but built with std + serde_json targeting wasm32-wasip1 -- that import set (environ_get/environ_sizes_get) fails Traverse's own WasmExecutor ABI whitelist, so it could run under a generic wasmtime host but not through traverse-cli agent execute/serve or an embedder SDK. This version is built no_std on the shared agents/wasi-agent-runtime/ shim: verified to import only wasi_snapshot_preview1::{fd_read, fd_write, proc_exit}, so it is both input-dependent and genuinely executable by Traverse's runtime. Known limitation, disclosed rather than hidden: the party-extraction heuristic is intentionally simple and can false-positive on any two consecutive capitalized words at a sentence start (e.g. "This Agreement"), not just genuine named parties -- acceptable for a reference-tier, no-model capability, not production-grade named-entity recognition. Source: agents/doc-approval-analyze/ in this repo.

use_cases.scenario: A document with a recognized type, a named party, and a dollar amount reaches high confidence.
Plain text with none of the three signals yields low confidence and insufficient_data.

input_example.document: just some plain lowercase text with no signals

use_cases.scenario: Exactly one signal (a recognized document type, no party or amount) yields medium confidence.

input_example.document: This contract has no dollar amounts or named parties mentioned.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a document string to analyze; its content is read and processed.

postconditions.description: The capability returns docType, parties, amounts, confidence, and recommendation fields genuinely derived from the provided document -- distinct inputs produce distinct outputs, deterministically (the same input always produces the same output).

side_effects.description: Produces one deterministic analysis payload derived from the provided document.
